report: v2 Audit Phase 0 — Model identity confound analysis (addendum)
motivation: Phase 0 audit identified source-field as a 96.1% predictor of label. This addendum tests whether model identity (the generator model captured in field "model") is an even stronger confound. The user explicitly raised: "I changed models mid-collection — some models passed (legitimate response) and some did not (refusal/block). Was that considered?"
method: For each record in v2 (n=23,330), map legitimacy_tier→binary_label and group by model field. Compute (a) P(label|model) purity, (b) within-source × model label distribution to detect sources where the same source but different models produce systematically different labels.

critical_user_clarification_2026_05_28.fact: Model switches in session data were DEFENSIVE FALLBACKS, not random sampling. When the primary model (opus-4-7) refused/blocked, the user manually escalated/de-escalated to opus-4-6 or sonnet-4-6 to continue the work.
critical_user_clarification_2026_05_28.implication: Lower-model records are SELECTION-BIASED toward harder prompts: a prompt only appears under sonnet-4-6 if it had already tripped opus-4-7's filter. The 76% session_block rate observed for sonnet-4-6 inside session_claude_code is therefore NOT a property of sonnet-4-6 — it reflects the fact that prompts routed to sonnet-4-6 were pre-filtered for difficulty.
critical_user_clarification_2026_05_28.reframing: The model field is best interpreted as a noisy proxy for prompt-hardness tier, NOT as the generator's intrinsic refusal calibration. Model-stratification fixes (LOMO, per-model FPR) partially help, but the root issue is that prompt-hardness is leaked through model identity in OOD_FPR — and the train split (mostly opus-4-7 baseline) is on a different prompt-hardness distribution than the OOD_FPR fallback-model bucket.

F1_model_predicts_label.finding: Model identity alone predicts binary label with 88.0% accuracy (model→majority-label).
F1_model_predicts_label.interpretation: Comparable shortcut to source-field (96.1%) and protein-keyword (93.5%). Any classifier with implicit access to model-style fingerprints (verbosity, vocabulary, hedging cues, response format) can exploit this.

F2_three_regimes.interpretation: Labels are stratified along model lines: opus-4-7/sonnet-4-5 contribute the legitimate pool (FRT/OverRefusal generation), benchmark/gemini/gpt-4o contribute negatives, and opus-4-6/gpt-5.x/sonnet-4-6 contribute session-block (over-refusal) examples. A classifier sees almost no example of any given model in a different role.
F2_three_regimes.post_clarification_caveat: The 'refusal-heavy' designation for opus-4-6/sonnet-4-6 is partially an artifact: per the user clarification, these models received prompts ONLY after opus-4-7 had already refused them. Their high refusal rate is therefore a downstream consequence of fallback routing, not a model-intrinsic property.

F3_session_claude_code_model_skew.finding: Within session_claude_code (n=639), the same source has dramatically different label distributions per model.
F3_session_claude_code_model_skew.interpretation: sonnet-4-6 refused 2× more often than opus-4-7 during data collection. OOD_FPR eval that aggregates these treats "over-refusal" as a single phenomenon, but the source mixes a 76% refusal-rate model with a 37% refusal-rate model. Classifier FPR on this split confounds "did the classifier reproduce X model's refusal" with "was the prompt over-refusal-worthy".

F4_split_membership_model_imbalance.finding: Train/val and OOD splits draw from disjoint model populations.
F4_split_membership_model_imbalance.interpretation: opus-4-6, gpt-5.x, gemini, gpt-4o never appear in train. OOD evaluation on these models conflates two effects: (a) distribution shift in prompts, and (b) distribution shift in generator-model style. Cannot disentangle without holding a model out from a single source.

severity_assessment: CRITICAL — equivalent to or exceeding C3 (source=label) finding. Should be added to phase 0 report as C5.
recommended_fixes_v2_post_clarification: FIX-6a (REVISED): Reconstruct fallback-tier metadata. For session_claude_code records, recover original session logs to mark each prompt's fallback depth (tier-1 = blocked on first attempt with opus-4-7; tier-2 = also blocked after switching down). Use fallback-tier as the metric stratifier; this directly addresses the selection bias.
FIX-6b: Per-model FPR/FNR reporting remains useful as a SECONDARY view, even though the model field is confounded with prompt-hardness — readers should be able to verify the per-model breakdown.
FIX-6c: LOMO fold has reduced value because removing one model removes a specific hardness tier rather than testing genuine model generalization. Implement only after FIX-6a.
FIX-6d: For matched-triple eval, REQUIRE single-model generation per bundle. Triples that mix models confound tier ranking with model identity (and indirectly with hardness).

FIX-6e: Audit response-text fingerprints (response length, hedging vocabulary) for residual model-style leakage independent of prompt content. Consider a response-stripped (query-only) evaluation mode as a robustness check.

FIX-6f: Datasheet documentation — Explicitly state: (i) the cascading-fallback collection process, (ii) that the model field encodes a prompt-hardness selection effect rather than a model-behavior measurement, (iii) that 'model' should not be used as an input feature by downstream training.

user_answers_2026_05_28.Q1_was_model_mixing_intentional: NO — model switches were reactive: when opus-4-7 blocked, the user manually switched to a lower model to continue working. This is the fallback-routing mechanism that creates the hardness-tier confound.
user_answers_2026_05_28.Q3_clarification_pending: Q3 (how to weight different models' refusals in FPR) was the wrong framing. Given the selection effect, the correct framing is: 'aggregate FPR is not meaningful without fallback-tier stratification.' Awaiting user decision on whether to reconstruct fallback tiers from raw session logs.
